name: Chrome Children: Growing Up Augmented in the Stack
creator: Amara Dziedzic-Nakashima
description: An oral history collecting testimonies from forty-seven people who received their first augmentations as children in Tier 1-2 stack housing, exploring what it meant to grow up with chrome in communities that couldn't afford proper maintenance, calibration, or medical oversight. Dziedzic-Nakashima spent four years conducting interviews and the resulting text is structured as a polyphonic chorus, with minimal editorial intrusion. The book does not offer solutions or policy recommendations; it simply insists on being heard.
medium: neural feed text (primary); physical paperback (community-funded print run of 1,500)
cultural_impact: Published only four years ago but already cited as a landmark document in augmentation rights advocacy; its testimony about under-maintained childhood implants causing long-term neurological effects has been submitted as evidence in two ongoing class-action suits against BCI manufacturers.
controversy: Three of the forty-seven interviewees have since recanted or claimed their words were misrepresented, leading to allegations that at least one was pressured to do so by a corporate legal team. Dziedzic-Nakashima has released the original unedited recordings for all three, which appear to support the published text.
story_hooks: One of the three recanting interviewees has reached out privately to Dziedzic-Nakashima — they want to retract their recantation and have evidence of the corporate pressure, but they're frightened.

A name appears in the testimony of multiple unrelated interviewees — a street-level chrome-repair technician who helped dozens of children in one the Gray Zone sector, who then disappeared in 2218 and has never been found.

The community-funded print run was financed through a series of small donations that, when traced, form a pattern suggesting a coordinated effort by someone who wanted this book to exist in physical form specifically — and that someone had resources inconsistent with Tier 1-2 origins.
